searchText: There is a currently pending situation that must be resolved in the specs, which is returning `stateless_validation=False` if the bytes received as input can’t be SSZ-deserialised. Currently, the guest program panics and the current strategy is to lean towards `stateless_validation=False` to have a clear path failure. The twist in this case, is that although we could set `stateless_validation=False` , [StatelessValidationResult](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/projects/zkevm/src/ethereum/forks/amsterdam/stateless.py) also has `new_payload_request_root` and `chain_config` fields which we can’t meaningfully set since we couldn’t even deserialize the input. I think there are at least two obvious options: - Option 1: Set `stateless_validation=False`, `new_payload_request_root=0x00..` and `chain_config = all-fields-zero-values` - Option 2: redefine `new_payload_request_root` and `chain_config` as optionals, and serialize these as SSZ List with max length 1. (Or an extra variant is create a wrapper to only have a single Optional that inside has those two fields). This situation of an invalid SSZ would be very weird, and I can hardly imagine those proofs even being sent to the network, but we should still define it. Maybe option 1 is fine, since not overcomplicating the SSZ API with a case that probably won't happen. I’m planning to resolve this case *somehow,* since we should — we can also lean on an option now and reconsider later, ofc; just opening this if anyone has any strong opinion or preference. If we always check the statelessValidation Boolean before doing anything else, then would option 1 be fine? So in general, if the Boolean is false, then the chain config etc can be anything Yep. If you first check the boolean, then there is no ambiguity on how to interpret the other two values. we currently have problems with exception handling, so our guest panics in such cases. that's the cause of those 12 eest tests failures -- execution-wise things are alright, just for some invalid scenarios it panics instead of returning a status of failure Ah, sounds good. I think prob that problem catching panic on your side might be something solvable? (i.e. prob related with many of hte compilation magics you have to do for .net ? ) it is solvable, but at the cost of performance. something to contemplate about internally.

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content:
There is a currently pending situation that must be resolved in the specs, which is returning `stateless_validation=False` if the bytes received as input can’t be SSZ-deserialised. Currently, the guest program panics and the current strategy is to lean towards `stateless_validation=False` to have a clear path failure.

The twist in this case, is that although we could set `stateless_validation=False` , [StatelessValidationResult](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/projects/zkevm/src/ethereum/forks/amsterdam/stateless.py) also has `new_payload_request_root` and `chain_config` fields which we can’t meaningfully set since we couldn’t even deserialize the input.

I think there are at least two obvious options:

- Option 1: Set `stateless_validation=False`, `new_payload_request_root=0x00..`  and `chain_config = all-fields-zero-values`
- Option 2: redefine `new_payload_request_root` and `chain_config` as optionals, and serialize these as SSZ List with max length 1. (Or an extra variant is create a wrapper to only have a single Optional that inside has those two fields).

This situation of an invalid SSZ would be very weird, and I can hardly imagine those proofs even being sent to the network, but we should still define it. Maybe option 1 is fine, since not overcomplicating the SSZ API with a case that probably won't happen. I’m planning to resolve this case *somehow,* since we should — we can also lean on an option now and reconsider later, ofc; just opening this if anyone has any strong opinion or preference.

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: If we always check the statelessValidation Boolean before doing anything else, then would option 1 be fine?

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: So in general, if the Boolean is false, then the chain config etc can be anything

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content: Yep. If you first check the boolean, then there is no ambiguity on how to interpret the other two values.

excerpts.content: we currently have problems with exception handling, so our guest panics in such cases. that's the cause of those 12 eest tests failures -- execution-wise things are alright, just for some invalid scenarios it panics instead of returning a status of failure
